ncu9gigwhi In trade, I compare opportunity costs: North gives up 0.5 electronics per unit of wheat versus 2 for South, so a relative price between the two can create a mutual gain. The aggregate gain doesn't say that every specific factor gains. In a second-price auction with private values, my bid decides whether I win but the best rival sets the payment; bidding my value is weakly dominant. That proof doesn't automatically hold for first price or with a common value. Finally, a snack trade can improve both utilities without yet being efficient if another mutually profitable trade remains feasible.
